translation: Yet there is also the theory of treating disease and removing eight or nine parts of it. Extending this, if it is extremely shallow it can be treated, but if deep it cannot be treated. When the disease reaches the point of being untreatable, there are those who fold their hands and wait for the end, and there are also those who want to stop but cannot; is this not a regret of life? Suppose there is a good physician who can both treat the disease and remove the root of the disease, so that the one suffering sees it and is pleased; even if he dies, he has no regret. How much more can he, turning around, not die? How much more can he from this attain longevity? What fortune is like this! What joy is like this! How not to die? Remove the disease. How to attain longevity? Remove the root of the disease. How to remove the root? Remove the accumulation (積). How to remove the accumulation? There is one word that can be practiced for a lifetime, and it is called “rubbing” (揉).
